Since the issue raised in these writ petitions are common, with the consent of the learned counsel appearing for the both sides, these writ petitions were heard together and are disposed of by this common order.
2. Invariably, the lands belonging to the petitioners were acquired by the respondent authority for the establishment of a Central University by the respondent State.

Insofar as the compensation payable to the petitioner and others, compensation has been paid, subsequently for the enhancement of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.1331, 1339 & 1336 of 2023 compensation, the land owners approached the appropriate authority and the compensation has been enhanced.

Accordingly, under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, the enhanced amount,
in fact, also was sought to be paid by the respondent to the petitioner.
3. However, they paid only the enhanced compensation, though it is a belated one, the interest has not been paid.

Therefore, in order to get the interest, the petitioners had given representations independently on 01.07.2022 to the respondent authority and in order to consider the said representations and to do the needful on merits and in accordance with law within a time frame to be stipulated by this Court, these petitioners have moved the respective writ petitions.
4. Reiterating the aforesaid, Ms.S.Harshitha, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner seeks indulgence of this Court.

5. Heard Mr.P.S.Kothandaraman, learned Government Advocate (P) appearing for the respondents,
who would submit that, the representations submitted by the petitioners individually would be considered and decided by the respondent authority on merits and in accordance with law within a time frame, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.1331, 1339 & 1336 of 2023 that may be stipulated by this Court.

sentences.text:
Considering the said submissions made by the learned Government Advocate (P), appearing for the respondents and taking note of the innocuous nature of the prayer sought for in these writ petitions, this Court is inclined to dispose of these writ petitions with the following orders:
That there shall be a direction to the respondent authority to consider the representations individually submitted by the petitioners dated 01.07.2022 and decide the same on merits and in accordance with law and pass necessary orders thereon within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
7.
With these directions, these writ petitions are disposed of.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
There will be no order as to costs.
